description: AI-enabled biological design requires stronger validation access control and governance.
Powerful design tools can lower barriers to harmful biological applications.
Environmental biotechnology may behave unpredictably outside controlled settings.
Heritable editing raises consent intergenerational and social legitimacy risks.
Agricultural biotechnology may concentrate control and reinforce monoculture.
Pathogen surveillance can improve preparedness but may create privacy stigma or geopolitical misuse.
Bio-based production may externalize land energy water or waste harms.
Cell and gene therapies may widen health inequality if access remains limited.
